skill.name: extract-from-pdfs
skill.description: Extract structured data from scientific PDFs for systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and research databases.
skill.summary: Turn scientific PDF collections into validated, exportable research datasets.
skill.author: brunoasm

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, placeholder secrets, output file writes, SQLite exports, and ordinary identifiers. Confirmed issues are the curl-to-shell Ollama installer instruction, API key persistence in a shell profile, external processing of PDFs or extracted values, and plain HTTP validation endpoints. No prompt injection attempt or stealthy data-exfiltration instruction was found.

remediation.issue: The setup guide pipes a remote Ollama installer directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell command with package manager instructions or a download, verification, and explicit execution flow.

remediation.issue: The setup guide recommends appending ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to ~/.bashrc.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend session-scoped environment variables, a local secrets manager, or a gitignored dotenv file with clear file permission guidance.

remediation.issue: Some validation endpoints use plain HTTP and can expose query values or usernames.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS endpoints where supported, document third-party disclosure, and keep --skip-validation easy to use for sensitive datasets.

remediation.issue: Claude and validation API workflows can transmit PDF content, abstracts, or extracted values externally.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy notice before API steps and recommend local Ollama filtering or offline processing when data is confidential.

content.value_statement: Scientific PDF collections are hard to convert into analysis-ready datasets. This skill guides metadata organization, schema-based extraction, validation, and export workflows.
actual_capabilities: Organizes paper metadata from BibTeX, RIS, DOI lists, or PDF directories.
Filters abstracts with Claude or a local Ollama model before full extraction.
Extracts schema-defined fields from scientific PDFs using Claude vision workflows.
Repairs and validates extracted JSON outputs against a user-defined schema.
Enriches extracted values through GBIF, WFO, GeoNames, PubChem, and NCBI APIs.
Exports results to CSV, Excel, SQLite, Python, R, and validation reports.
limitations: Claude-based extraction requires an Anthropic API key and may send PDF content to Anthropic.
Validation APIs may receive extracted species, location, compound, or gene values.
Extraction quality depends on PDF quality, schema clarity, and manual review.
The skill is built for research data extraction, not general PDF editing or search.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Systematic Review Dataset
use_cases.description: Convert a literature corpus into structured fields for screening, extraction, and downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Build a Research Database
use_cases.description: Standardize metadata, extract domain-specific records, validate values, and export a reusable database.

use_cases.title: Validate Scientific Entities
use_cases.description: Check extracted taxonomy, geography, chemistry, or gene values against public reference APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Start a PDF Extraction Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new literature corpus.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan extraction from my scientific PDFs. Ask what metadata I have, what fields I need, and which outputs I want.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Extraction Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a schema for extracting structured data from example papers. Use two sample PDFs and list required fields, optional fields, and validation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Extraction Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute the main workflow with checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through organizing metadata, filtering abstracts, extracting from PDFs, repairing outputs, and exporting the final dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Compare Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a validation set, calculate precision, recall, and F1 scores, then suggest schema or prompt changes based on the weakest fields.

output_examples.input: A folder of ecology papers plus a schema for plant, visitor, location, and observation fields.
output_examples.output: A cleaned dataset with paper identifiers, extracted interaction records, validated taxonomy fields, and a short quality report.

output_examples.input: A BibTeX library and abstracts for 500 candidate papers in a systematic review.
output_examples.output: A filtered paper list with relevance decisions, reasons, model metadata, and a summary of papers selected for full extraction.

output_examples.input: Validated extraction results and a manually annotated validation sample.
output_examples.output: Precision, recall, and F1 metrics by field, plus recommendations for improving low-performing fields.

best_practices: Review two or three representative PDFs before finalizing the extraction schema.
Run test mode on a small sample before processing the full corpus.
Create a validation set and report field-level metrics before using results in analysis.
anti_patterns: Running full extraction before customizing the schema and filtering criteria.
Sending confidential PDFs or sensitive extracted values to APIs without approval.
Treating automated extraction results as ground truth without manual validation.

faq.question: Can this skill process any PDF?
faq.answer: It is designed for scientific papers with extractable research data. Scanned or poorly formatted PDFs may need manual review.

faq.question: Does it require an Anthropic API key?
faq.answer: Yes for Claude PDF extraction and Claude-based filtering. Ollama can be used locally for abstract filtering only.

faq.question: Can I use this with Codex or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill runners.

faq.question: What data may leave my machine?
faq.answer: Claude steps may send PDF content or abstracts to Anthropic. Validation steps may send extracted values to public APIs.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The scripts can export cleaned records to CSV, Excel, SQLite, Python, R, and validation report files.

faq.question: How should I check accuracy?
faq.answer: Sample papers for manual annotation, fill ground truth fields, and calculate precision, recall, and F1 metrics.
